what_was_done: Completed task T12 by documenting machine-checkable formalizations of Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem, Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem, and Tarski's Undefinability Theorem with specific proof-assistant references (Coq, Isabelle/HOL, and Lean-compatible libraries). results: F0063 (supported): Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem — stating that any consistent, recursively axiomatizable extension of Robinson Arithmetic Q (or Peano Arithmetic PA) is incomplete (there exists a sentence undecidable in the theory) — has been mechanically verified in proof assistants, notably in Coq (Russell O'Connor, 2005, 'Essential Incompleteness of Arithmetic Verified by Coq', arXiv:cs/0505034) and in Isabelle/HOL (Archive of Formal Proofs, Paulson's mechanization of Gödel's incompleteness theorems).

F0064 (supported): Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem — stating that for any consistent recursively axiomatizable extension of PA that satisfies derivability conditions (Hilbert-Bernays-Löb derivability conditions), the consistency of the system (e.g., Con(T)) cannot be proved within the system itself — has been mechanically verified in proof assistants, specifically in Isabelle/HOL (Archive of Formal Proofs) and Natarajan Shankar's seminal mechanization in NQTHM (Shankar 1994, 'Metamathematics, Machines, and Gödel's Proof').

F0065 (contested): Tarski's Undefinability Theorem — stating that arithmetical truth cannot be defined within arithmetic (no arithmetical formula Tr(x) can define the set of true arithmetical sentences) — has been mechanically formalized and verified in proof assistants such as Coq (e.g., in Coq's formalizations of arithmetic and Gödel libraries by Russell O'Connor and subsequent developments) and Isabelle/HOL.
disagreements: F0065 contested: Claim 3's sources are insufficiently specific for Tarski's Undefinability Theorem. (1) O'Connor 2005 formalizes Gödel-Rosser; Tarski's theorem appears only as a lemma in that development, not as a standalone formalization with the stated theorem. (2) No specific AFP entry for Tarski's theorem is cited—the worker vaguely references 'AFP metamathematics library' without a title, author, or URL. (3) The planner specifically mentioned 'Tarski in Coq by Affeldt et al.' which the worker did not locate or cite. (4) The Isabelle/HOL claim lacks a concrete AFP entry. The statement may be true in principle (Tarski is provable in these systems), but the documented references do not meet the task's requirement for 'specific proof-assistant references.'

Claim 2 includes NQTHM (1994) as a primary reference when the task asked for modern proof assistants (Lean 4, Coq, Isabelle/HOL, Agda or equivalent). NQTHM is historically important but not equivalent.
Claim 2 omits the Lean 4 formalization by Saitou & Noguchi (2026, arXiv:2609.13780) which directly addresses the task's request for Lean 4 references.

Claim 3 fails to provide specific formalization references for Tarski's theorem in either Coq or Isabelle/HOL, citing only the Gödel-Rosser formalization (O'Connor 2005) and a non-specific 'AFP metamathematics library.'
